newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Big radiation increase in ruined Chernobyl reactor.
newsitem.headline: Big radiation increase in ruined Chernobyl reactor.

text.p: Radiation levels inside the Chernobyl nuclear power plant's ruined fourth reactor rose sharply this week and a director said on Tuesday specialists were investigating whether this could eventually cause a chain reaction.

Valentyn Kupny, in charge of the "sarcophagus" surrounding the reactor, said meters inside the cracking steel and concrete structure had shown big increases for a time on Monday. He said scientists did not have full control over the mass of nuclear fuel still inside 10 years after the reactor exploded.

Kupny said readings on three of 10 meters showed increases in neutron radiation inside the sarcophagus (protective casing), hurriedly erected after the fourth reactor exploded on April 26, 1986 and sent radiation over much of Europe. He said a commission had been set up to examine the incident, the third in the past 10 years.

"The latest increases were temporary. No final conclusions were drawn from the earlier instances whether a chain reaction had been started," Kupny said by telephone from Chernobyl, 140 km (90 miles) north of Kiev.
"Everything that is inside has not been fully studied or understood. We do not have a sufficiently complete control system."

Experts differ on how much fuel remains inside the reactor, with estimates ranging from 90 to 160 tonnes. A Western-backed project to build a new sarcophagus was first made public three years ago but no specific steps have yet been taken to build it.
